reading.body:
CIN2 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity across 143,778 square feet, which at typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack translates to roughly 275 racks as an assumption about configuration. The campus qualifies to host workloads requiring PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II compliance. It ranks third among the eight facilities in Ohio with published power capacity, holding 18 percent of the state's declared 60.4 MW.

Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities on record, but only eight publish IT capacity figures, making CIN2 one of the few sites in the state with transparent power specifications. The state's total published capacity of 60.4 MW places it at the lower end of AI infrastructure density compared to major compute hubs, though the actual footprint may be larger if unmapped or undisclosed facilities exist.

For an AI operator seeking east-of-Mississippi capacity with compliance certifications, CIN2 represents accessible infrastructure within a modest regional market. Whether 11 MW matters depends on workload type and tenant strategy: it is neither hyperscale nor negligible, and sits within a state where the grid and power supply have not yet become visible constraints in published facility announcements.
